{{Short description|Scottish musician (born 1959)}} {{Distinguish|Colin Edwin}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use British English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Edwyn Collins | image = Edwyn Collins, 2019-09-27.jpg | caption = Collins in 2019 | background = solo_singer | birth_name = Edwyn Stephen Collins | alias = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|df=yes|1959|8|23}} | birth_place = [[Edinburgh]], Scotland | origin = [[Dundee]], Scotland | death_date = | instrument = {{hlist|Vocals|guitar|bass|violin|synthesizer|[[Sampler (musical instrument)|sampling]]|drums|harmonica}} | genre = {{hlist|[[Alternative rock]]|[[post-punk]]|[[New wave music|new wave]]|[[indie pop]]}} | occupation = {{hlist|Singer-songwriter|musician|record label owner}} | years_active = {{hlist|1976–2005|2007–present}} | label = {{hlist|[[Setanta Records|Setanta]]|[[Epic Records|Epic]]|[[Heavenly Recordings|Heavenly]]|AED (Analogue Enhanced Digital)}} | past_member_of = {{hlist|[[Nu-Sonics]]|[[Orange Juice (band)|Orange Juice]]|[[The Drums]]|[[Aztec Camera]]|[[The Cribs]]|[[Roddy Frame]]}} | website = {{URL|edwyncollins.com}} }} '''Edwyn Stephen Collins''' (born 23 August 1959) is a Scottish musician, producer and record label owner. Collins was the lead singer for the 1980s [[post-punk]] band [[Orange Juice (band)|Orange Juice]], which he co-founded. After the group split in 1985, Collins started a solo career. His 1994 single "[[A Girl Like You (Edwyn Collins song)|A Girl Like You]]" was a worldwide hit. In February 2005, Collins was hospitalised after two cerebral haemorrhages which resulted in [[aphasia]], and he needed months to recover. He resumed his musical career in 2007.{{cite web| last1=Pollock|first1=David|title=The miraculous return of Edwyn Collins| url= https://www.theguardian.com/music/musicblog/2007/jul/04/edwyncollins|website=The Guardian|access-date=3 August 2016| date=4 July 2007}} A documentary film on his recovery, ''[[The Possibilities Are Endless]]'', was released in 2014. Collins was the co-founder of the indie record label [[Postcard Records]] and co-founded a second label, Analogue Enhanced Digital, in 2011. Collins has also worked as an illustrator, television actor, television producer and record producer. He won an [[Ivor Novello Award]], the Ivor Inspiration Award, in 2009.{{cite web| last1= Swash |first1= Rosie|title=Double triumph for Elbow at Ivor Novello Awards| url= https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/may/21/elbow-triumph-ivor-novello-awards|website=The Guardian|access-date=3 August 2016|date=21 May 2009}} ==Early life== Edwyn Stephen Collins was born on 23 August 1959 in [[Edinburgh]]. He lived in [[Dundee]] from the age of six to 14 after his father got a job as a lecturer at [[Duncan of Jordanstone College of Art and Design]]. He attended the now-defunct Demonstration School in Park Place, where new educational ideas were tried out by pupils and teachers from the adjacent teacher training college, before moving to the secondary school, [[Morgan Academy]].{{Cite web|url= https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/lifestyle/entertainment/music/rocktalk/965348/interview-strokes-left-me-so-vulnerable-says-music-star-edwyn-collins-ahead-of-dundee-homecoming-concert/|title=FEATURE: 'Strokes left me so vulnerable,' says Dundee-raised music star Edwyn Collins ahead of homecoming concert |website= Thecourier.co.uk|date=30 August 2019 |access-date=3 December 2019}} ==Career== ===Orange Juice=== {{main|Orange Juice (band)}} Collins co-founded the band the [[Nu-Sonics]] in 1976; The band changed its name to [[Orange Juice (band)|Orange Juice]] in 1979. Collins and his friend Alan Horne founded the record label [[Postcard Records]] that year to release the band's singles.{{cite web |title=Show 507 – Edwyn Collins Feature |url= https://soundcloud.com/britishcouncil/edwyn-collins-feature |website=SoundCloud |access-date=3 July 2014 |year=2011}} The band's debut single, "[[Falling and Laughing]]" was issued in February 1980. Although critically acclaimed, the single only sold 2,000 copies.{{cite web| last1=McKay| first1=Alastair|title=Orange Juice: "If anything became too smooth, Edwyn Collins liked to fuck it up" - Uncut| url= http://www.uncut.co.uk/features/orange-juice-if-anything-became-too-smooth-edwyn-collins-liked-to-fuck-it-up-7627| website=Uncut|access-date=3 August 2016|date=20 June 2014}} After three more singles with Postcard, Orange Juice signed to [[Polydor Records]] in October 1981 and released their debut album, ''[[You Can't Hide Your Love Forever]]'' in March 1982. The band's second album, ''[[Rip It Up (Orange Juice album)|Rip It Up]]'' followed in November 1982. Their single "[[Rip It Up (Orange Juice song)|Rip It Up]]", released in early 1983, reached number 8 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and was noted as the first British hit single to feature a bass-line from the [[Roland TB-303]] synthesizer.{{cite magazine |url= http://www.stylusmagazine.com/articles/seconds/buzzcocks-boredom-orange-juice-rip-it-up.htm |title=Buzzcocks: Boredom / Orange Juice: Rip It Up - Seconds |magazine=Stylus Magazine |access-date=7 September 2015 |archive-date=4 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604010309/http://stylusmagazine.com/articles/seconds/buzzcocks-boredom-orange-juice-rip-it-up.htm |url-status=dead }} The song was their only Top 40 single.{{cite web|title=ORANGE JUICE {{!}} full Official Chart History | publisher= Official Charts Company| url= http://www.officialcharts.com/artist/19352/orange-juice/| website= officialcharts.com}} The band's two subsequent albums, ''[[Texas Fever]]'' and ''[[The Orange Juice]]'', were both released in 1984. They failed to find the same success as ''Rip It Up''. Orange Juice disbanded in January 1985, after Polydor grew dissatisfied with the band's lack of success and the band's difficulty finding a new label to sign with. During this time in his career, Collins met Grace Maxwell, whom he hired as his manager and later married. Collins started his solo career in 1986, and signed to [[Elevation Records]], a label that was a co-venture between indie label [[Creation Records]] and major label [[Warner Music Group|Warner Music]].{{cite web|last=Ankeny |first=Jason |url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p45120/biography|pure_url=yes}} |title= Biography |website=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=26 July 2009}} ===Solo career to 2005=== Collins released two singles for the Elevation label in 1987, both produced by [[Robin Guthrie]] of the [[Cocteau Twins]], but both failed to enter the [[UK Singles Chart]]. Elevation was closed in November 1987, just ten months after it released its first single. After the closure, Collins experienced a "falling out" with [[Creation Records]] founder [[Alan McGee]], who had financed Elevation.{{cite web| title= Biography |url=https://music.apple.com/us/artist/edwyn-collins/3478219|website=iTunes Preview|publisher=Apple Inc|access-date= 3 July 2014|year=2014}} As a result, unlike other Elevation signees such as [[Primal Scream]] and [[The Weather Prophets]], Collins was not migrated to the main Creation label and he was left without a record label contract. At the request of passionate Orange Juice fans in Germany, Collins recorded his next album at a small German studio, with the aid of producer Dennis Bovell, who had worked with Collins in Orange Juice, and [[Roddy Frame]] of [[Aztec Camera]]. The album, ''[[Hope and Despair]]'', was released in 1989 by the Demon label and achieved success as an independent release. Demon also released Collins's next record, ''[[Hellbent on Compromise]]'' (1990), which was not as successful as its predecessor. Demon and Collins then parted ways and Collins embarked on a lengthy hiatus. Collins built his own recording studio in 1994 that was used to record his third solo album, ''[[Gorgeous George (album)|Gorgeous George]]'', which he also produced. The studio, located in [[West Hampstead]], London, would become the West Heath Yard Studios that Collins would use for his future record label, AED Records.{{cite web|title=AED Welcomes You|url= http://www.aedrecords.com/pages/about |website=AEDRecords.com |publisher=AED Records|access-date=3 July 2014|year=2012}} In 1994, Collins released the single "[[A Girl Like You (Edwyn Collins song)|A Girl Like You]]", which was a worldwide hit the following year. It became his only US hit, reaching number 32, after it was featured in the film ''[[Empire Records]]''. It was subsequently used in the movie ''[[Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle]]'' in 2003. Collins released his followup to ''Gorgeous George'', ''[[I'm Not Following You]]'', in 1997. One of its singles, "The Magic Piper (of Love)", was featured on the soundtrack for ''[[Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery]]'' that year ===Cerebral haemorrhage=== In a [[BBC 6 Music]] [[radio station|radio]] interview on 18 February 2005, Collins said he felt unwell, but ascribed the [[nausea]] and [[Vertigo (medical)|vertigo]] to [[food poisoning]].{{cite news| url= https://www.theguardian.com/music/2007/aug/17/popandrock1 |title='I was dead – and I was resurrected' |work= The Guardian |date= 17 August 2007|access-date=26 July 2009 | location=London | first=Simon | last=Goddard}} Two days later, he was admitted to [[intensive care]] in London's [[Royal Free Hospital]] after apparently suffering a major [[cerebral haemorrhage]].{{cite web| last1= Ferguson| first1= Euan|title=Edwyn Collins: 'I couldn't really talk. The words I could say were "yes", "no" and "the possibilities are endless"'|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/sep/28/edwyn-collins-musician-film-of-life-stroke|website=The Guardian|access-date=3 August 2016| date=28 September 2014}} After suffering a second haemorrhage he had an operation on 25 February 2005, which was followed by a lengthy programme of neurological rehabilitation owing to right-sided weakness and difficulty with speech. His [[aphasia]] left him able to repeat only four phrases: "yes", "no", "Grace Maxwell" (his wife's name) and "the possibilities are endless".{{cite web |last=Lewis |first=John |url=http://www.metro.co.uk/music/840674-edwyn-collins-back-with-a-vengeance |title=Edwyn Collins: Back with a vengeance |website=Metro.co.uk |date=12 September 2010 |access-date=30 March 2013 |archive-date=4 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004130404/http://www.metro.co.uk/music/840674-edwyn-collins-back-with-a-vengeance |url-status=dead }} ===Post-cerebral haemorrhage=== Collins released his sixth solo album, entitled ''[[Home Again (Edwyn Collins album)|Home Again]]'', in September 2007 on [[Heavenly Records]]. The album was [[sound recording and reproduction|recorded]] before his illness but mixed after his discharge from hospital. While still recovering, Collins returned to singing live, including playing a [[concert|gig]] at The Arts Theatre in London. A tribute song celebrating his return was recorded by the [[indie pop]] band The Candy Twins.{{cite web| url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wZzN34nSYH4 |archive-url= https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/wZzN34nSYH4 | archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|title=The Candy Twins Edwyn Collins is Back (tribute song) |website=Uk.youtube.com |date=25 February 2007 |access-date=26 July 2009}}{{cbignore}} A [[BBC Scotland]] [[film documentary|documentary]], ''Edwyn Collins: Home Again'', narrated by [[Franz Ferdinand (band)|Franz Ferdinand]] frontman [[Alex Kapranos]], was broadcast on 19 May 2008. Filmed during 2007, it follows Collins's progress in recovering from his illness and his first return to live performance at the BBC [[Electric Proms]]. Collins then performed at the [[Glastonbury Festival]], which was broadcast on 28 June 2008 on [[BBC Two]], and at [[T in the Park]] on 10 July 2009 (Collins's first ever T in the Park).{{cite web|title=Daily Record @ T in the Park: Edwyn Collins & Franz Ferdinand|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=646Ng-oyYYs |archive-url= https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/646Ng-oyYYs| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live| publisher= scottishdailyrecord | via= YouTube| access-date=3 July 2014|format=Video upload|date=10 July 2009}}{{cbignore}} On 2 October 2009, Collins's wife and manager Grace Maxwell detailed her "running battle" with [[Warner Music Group]] and MySpace over his right to allow fans to listen to "A Girl Like You" for free on his MySpace page.{{cite web|url= http://www.nme.com/news/edwyn-collins/47628|title=Edwyn Collins' manager blasts MySpace and major labels over 'A Girl Like You' |publisher=NME |date=2 October 2009 |access-date=7 October 2009}} In November 2009, at a gig in London's Bloomsbury Ballroom, following a tour of the Scottish Highlands, Collins's singing was contrasted with his slow speech: "[W]hen he started to sing, his baritone proved as powerful as ever."{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/musician-heal-thyself-1.797695 |title=Musician, heal thyself |access-date=20 October 2009 | work=CBC News}} On 20 February 2010, he joined [[The Maccabees (band)|The Maccabees]] onstage at Brixton Academy for their encore, performing vocals on a rendition of "Rip It Up". ''Losing Sleep'', Collins's first written and recorded album since his 2005 illness, was then released on 13 September 2010 in the UK.{{cite web| title=Edwyn Collins new album and download track 'Losing Sleep'| url= http://heavenlyrecordings.com/news/2010/07/edwyn-collins-new-album-download-track-losing-sleep/|website= HeavenlyRecordings.com | publisher= Heavenly Recordings|access-date=3 July 2014|date=21 July 2010|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140714183734/http://heavenlyrecordings.com/news/2010/07/edwyn-collins-new-album-download-track-losing-sleep/|archive-date=14 July 2014}} The album was recorded at his own West Heath Studios between November 2008 and May 2010, and was produced by Collins and Sebastian Lewsley. Collins and Lewsley first met in 1992, while Collins was producing former [[Subway Sect]] frontman [[Vic Godard]]'s album ''The End of the Surrey People'' and Lewsley was his assistant. For the album, he collaborated with The Cribs' Ryan Jarman and [[Johnny Marr]], Franz Ferdinand, [[The Magic Numbers]] singer Romeo Stodart, [[the Drums]] and [[Roddy Frame]].{{cite web|title=Edwyn Collins|url= http://heavenlyrecordings.com/artists/edwyn-collins/ | website= HeavenlyRecordings.com| publisher= Heavenly Recordings|access-date=3 July 2014 |year=2010|url-status=dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140711052032/http://heavenlyrecordings.com/artists/edwyn-collins/|archive-date=11 July 2014}} Lewsley explained the recording process of ''Losing Sleep'' in 2010:
We did each song in a day ... and a day consists of about four hours. So there's a real expediency about how it's recorded. The whole attitude of the album is just doing that. Not indulging anyone. Not having any band sitting round for days and days. "Have you got a guitar part yet? No? Just do it. You've got a coupla hours." They [Collins's collaborators] all looked quite petrified but they did it.
In 2009, during the making of ''Losing Sleep'', Lewsley observed Collins gradually regain his musical proficiency—Lewsley explained: "The studio is more of an instrument again for Edwyn." The cover art for the album features a collection of bird drawings that Collins started working on in 2005. On 30 September 2010, Collins and his band broadcast three live songs from the Royal Beacon Hotel in [[Exmouth]] for [[BBC Radio 2]]'s "[[Radcliffe and Maconie Show]]".{{cite web| url= http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00bch8n |title=BBC Radio 2 – The Radcliffe and Maconie Show, 30/09/2010, Edwyn Collins – Losing Sleep and What Is My Role | website=BBC.co.uk |date=30 September 2010 |access-date=30 March 2013}} ([[Stuart Maconie]] is a former [[music journalist]] and his first ''[[NME]]'' article was a review of Collins's 1987 gig at the Manchester International.){{cite book| first= Stuart| last= Maconie| year= 2004| title= Cider With Roadies| edition= 1st| publisher= Random House | location= London| isbn= 0-09-189115-9| page= 182}} On 30 July 2011, Collins performed at the [[Indietracks]] festival that was held at the Midland Railway, [[Butterley]].{{cite web| last1= Jack| first1= Malcolm| title=Indietracks – review| url= https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2011/aug/02/indietracks-festival-review| work= The Guardian | date= 2 August 2011|access-date=11 August 2016}} During the 2012 Kendal Calling event Collins sang "A Girl Like You", with Roddy Frame on guitar and [[Tim Burgess (artist)|Tim Burgess]] on backing vocals.{{cite web|title=Edwyn Collins, Tim Burgess and Roddy Frame- A Girl Like You (At Tim Peaks- Kendal Calling 2012)| url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pku0Pb4Espw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/pku0Pb4Espw| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|via=YouTube| publisher= tunafishmediavideos |access-date=17 April 2014 |format=Video |date=4 August 2012}}{{cbignore}} Collins's eighth solo album, ''Understated'', was released in March 2013 on his own AED Records label and was critically well received, with ''God Is in the TV'' stating:
Understated is more than just another step to recovery, it is indeed a fine record in its own right, and utterly life-affirming. It's also perhaps the ultimate testament to the healing power of music. He lost the ability to read, write, and lost movement in half of his body, but what he didn't lose was his gift for coming up with an ear-catching tune, as is proved here. It will make you smile, it may even make you cry, and it's an album that reminds you how good it is to be alive.{{cite web| first=Ben P| last= Scott |url= http://www.godisinthetvzine.co.uk/2013/03/29/edwyn-collins-understated-aed-records/ |title=Review: Edwyn Collins – Understated (AED Records) |work= Godisinthetvzine.co.uk |date=29 March 2013 |access-date=24 May 2013}}
A documentary film about Collins entitled ''The Possibilities Are Endless'', directed by James Hall and Edward Lovelace, was released in November 2014.{{cite web |url= http://www.thepossibilities.co.uk/about.html |title=The Possibilities Are Endless |work=thepossibilities.co.uk |year=2014 |access-date=14 November 2014}}{{cite web |url= https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3512066/ |title=The Possibilities Are Endless |work=IMDb |year=2014 |access-date=14 November 2014}} ==Collaborations with Roddy Frame== Collins has been friends with [[Roddy Frame]], the frontman for the new wave group [[Aztec Camera]], since they were both signed to Postcard Records in the 1980s.{{cite web|title=Roddy Frame chats to Stuart Maconie|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p01wk20s|work=Radcliffe and Maconie on BBC Radio 6|publisher=BBC|access-date=17 April 2014|format=Audio upload|date=31 March 2014}} Collins and Frame collaborated on the Aztec Camera album ''Stray'', including a live performance of the song "Consolation Prize".{{cite web|title=Aztec Camera Stray – Credits|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/stray-mw0000689857/credits|work=Aztec Camera on AllMusic|publisher=All Media Network, LLC|access-date=17 April 2014|year=2014}} Frame performed with Collins in November 2007 during Collins's first concert after his recovery from a serious illness,{{cite news |title=The Soulful Survivor|url=http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/music/gig-23371370-details/Edwyn+Collins,+Vic+Godard+And+The+Subway+Sect/gigReview.do?reviewId=23421983&expand=true|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605182451/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/music/review-23421983-the-soulful-survivor.do|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 June 2011|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|date=20 November 2007|access-date=15 March 2008}} and the pair played again at the [[Glastonbury Festival 2008|Glastonbury Festival]] in June 2008, on the Park Stage, and at the Purcell Rooms in London, UK, in September 2008.{{cite web|title=Glastonbury Festival 2008|url=http://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/photo-of-edwyn-collins-and-roddy-frame-roddy-frame-news-photo/85112081|work=Getty Images|access-date=17 April 2014|author=Hayley Madden|date=26 February 2009 |format=Image upload}}{{cite web|title=A GIRL LIKE YOU EDWYN COLLINS PURCELL ROOMS SEPT 14 2008|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ib5hnzOnXFg |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/ib5hnzOnXFg| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|website=David Yeates on YouTube|publisher=Google Inc|access-date=22 June 2014|format=Video upload|date=14 September 2008}}{{cbignore}} Frame's fourth solo album, ''Seven Dials'', was released in 2014 on Collins's AED record label. Frame explained, following the album's release, that he had been inspired to make an album with a full band after his positive experience playing with Collins in 2007 and 2008.{{cite web|title=With Roddy Frame|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b044v68w|website=The Tom Robinson Show|publisher=BBC|access-date=21 June 2014|format=Audio upload|date=24 May 2014}} ==Production work== Collins has also worked extensively as a record producer with other artists, including Terrorvision, [[Robert Forster (musician)|Robert Forster]], [[The Cribs]], [[Little Barrie]], [[Hooton Tennis Club]] and Vic Godard. In 1999, Collins was invited by the band [[Space (English band)|Space]] to produce what would have been their third album ''[[Love You More than Football]]'', which ended up being scrapped. However he is credited as a producer on a few B-sides, and he delivers a brief vocal cameo on the song "Thank You", where he makes reference to "Falling and Laughing". In 2005 Collins produced the Cribs album ''[[The New Fellas]]'' and co-produced the 2013 album ''Clarietta'', by Charlie Boyer and the Voyeurs, with Lewsley. He also co-produced [[The Rails]]' debut album ''Fair Warning'', released on [[Island Records]] in 2014.{{cite web | url= https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/jan/10/the-rails-new-band-of-the-day | title=The Rails (New band of the day No 1,675 | work=[[The Guardian]] | date=10 January 2014 | access-date=23 April 2015 | last=Lester | first=Paul | author-link=Paul Lester}} Collins also produced ''The Official Body'', the third album by the British post-punk band [[Shopping (band)|Shopping]], which was released on 19 January 2018.{{cite web|title=Shopping announce new LP 'The Official Body,' share "The Hype"|url=http://www.brooklynvegan.com/shopping-announce-new-lp-the-official-body-share-the-hype/|website=BrooklynVegan|access-date=20 January 2018}} Collins co-produced a collaborative project between [[Camera Obscura (band)|Camera Obscura]] frontwoman [[Tracyanne Campbell]] and guitarist [[Danny Coughlan]] that was released in May 2018 by [[Merge Records]] with the title Tracyanne & Danny. ==Other projects== In addition to his music career Collins also produced and starred in the [[Channel 4]] television show ''West Heath Yard''.{{cite web|author1=Matt Frost|title=Edwyn Collins: Recording Losing Sleep|url=http://www.soundonsound.com/sos/jan11/articles/edwyn-collins.htm|website=Sound on Sound|publisher=SOS Publications Group|access-date=3 July 2014|date=January 2011}} Collins released his first book of illustrations, ''Some British Birds'', with Morel Books in 2009.{{cite book|author1=Edwyn Collins|title=Some British Birds|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JfhDXwAACAAJ|publisher=Google Inc|access-date=3 July 2014|year=2009|isbn=9781907071072}} [[Liberty (department store)|Liberty of London]] printed his bird illustrations on fabric as part of a series of fabrics created in collaboration with musicians; his print is named Ornithology.{{Cite news|url=https://www.creativereview.co.uk/liberty-rocks/|title=Liberty Rocks - Creative Review|date=20 July 2011|work=Creative Review|access-date=20 November 2017|language=en-US}} ==Awards and honours== In May 2009 Collins won the [[Ivor Novello award|Ivors Inspiration Award]] in recognition of his struggles following his 2005 [[Cerebral hemorrhage|brain haemorrhage]]. *1995: [[Goldene Europa]] for Best International Singer *1996: [[Ivor Novello Awards|Ivor Novello Award]] for Most Performed Work & Best Contemporary Song ("[[A Girl Like You (Edwyn Collins song)|A Girl Like You]]") (nominated) *1996: RSH Gold Awards for Airplay Hit of the Year ("[[A Girl Like You (Edwyn Collins song)|A Girl Like You]]") *2008: [[UK Festival Awards|UK Festival Award]] for Festival Feel-Good Act & Year Award]] for ''[[Understated (Edwyn Collins album)|Understated]]'' (nominated) *2019, [[Scottish Album of the Year Award]] (Longlisted) for ''Badbea'' (nominated) In 2010, he received an honorary 2010, Collins attended the Helmsdale Highland Games as the chieftain, an honour also previously bestowed on his grandfather.{{cite web|url=http://www.helmsdalegames.info/This_Years_Chieftain.html|title=This Years Chieftain 2010|publisher=Helmsdalegames.info|access-date=22 September 2014}} On 24 August 2022, Collins appeared on Glasgow|website=Glasgow Times|date=August 23, 2012}} ==Personal life== Collins is married to Grace Maxwell, who is also his manager. The couple live in [[Helmsdale]].{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/home-news/collins-faces-fight-to-build-highland-recording-studio.20448544 |title=Collins faces fight to build
